findings.description: Test adequacy: dropping `-c core.commitGraph=false` from `descendsFrom` passes every test, though commit 931ebb7 adds it so a forged commit graph cannot answer the ancestry check.

The refusal without --accept-head offers the compare link and the exact `pup land <id> --accept-head <head>` command before anything checks that the head descends from the pin, and that check (descendsFrom) only runs later under the lock. Trigger: a fix round rebased the PR branch (ADR 0164 names this case) and GitHub merged it. The operator gets a compare view against the merge-base, which hides that the pinned commits were rewritten, and is told to run a command that is then always refused under the lock. ADR 0164 lines 30-31 make the same claim ("the view shows exactly the commits past it") and are just as unchecked at that point.

The only accepted-head land test is a merge commit, so `deleteBranchIfHeld`'s `targetSha` already holds the branch. Reverting `tearDown(…, head)` to `tearDown(…, sha)` passes every test, and a squash or rebase merge at an accepted head would then keep the branch the ADR says is deleted.

process_issues.description: A Grep over the repository root was denied, so the guards reviewer searched only src/ for source-scanning guard tests and did not cover scripts/ or top-level test directories.
